solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A politician lied, oddly enough

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the standard crossword politician

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word lied

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a politician has told a lie, which is hardly surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' reads as a phrase, but 'oddly' is the selection signal and 'enough' is the definition: L and E are the first and third letters of 'lied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, as much as is needed, a close synonym of enough.

clue.text: Assumed name lacks heart, unfortunately

indicators.note: the centre letter of the five-letter word for an assumed name is dropped

parts.note: an alias is a false or assumed name

explanation.surface: A fake identity turns out to be hollow, which is a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the middle I from ALIAS leaves the interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, said where one might say sadly or unfortunately.

clue.text: Pay up front to be getting on section of website

indicators.note: up front points to the opening letter of the word Pay

parts.note: to age is to grow older, to be getting on in years

explanation.surface: Advice to pay in advance before getting started with part of a website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' sounds like advance payment, but it only selects the first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A web page is a single document within a website, one of its sections.

clue.text: Former wife in St. Helier, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unstated way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former wife now lives in St Helier, by some means.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helier is the capital of Jersey, a Channel Island; its letters with W are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is a literary adjective meaning previous or one-time, exactly like former.

clue.text: Irritated and out of bed following injury

indicators.note: following places the word for out of bed after the word for injury

parts.note: a wound is an injury
someone who is up has risen from bed

explanation.surface: Someone is cross and has got up after hurting themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Wound up is an informal idiom for agitated or annoyed, a state of being irritated.

clue.text: Money made by breaking the law

indicators.note: breaking suggests the phrase is smashed apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A fortune obtained through crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking the law' reads as one idiom, but 'breaking' is the anagram signal for THE LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth is an abundance of riches, so money stands for it in a loose synonym.

clue.text: Be paid, reportedly, for pot

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, so the answer sounds like the word for being paid

parts.note: to earn is to be paid for work

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be paid for making a piece of pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent EARN and URN sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a large vase or vessel, a kind of pot.

clue.text: After ten years, books degraded

indicators.note: After puts the books abbreviation at the end, behind the ten-year word

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A decade on, some books have deteriorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline and self-indulgence, a state of being degraded.

clue.text: Expecting power in control

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
regnant means reigning, in control

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates power and being in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is an everyday euphemism for carrying a baby, the condition of pregnancy.

clue.text: Majestic area somewhere in Georgia

parts.note: august means venerable, majestic

explanation.surface: A grand region located in the US state of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majestic' is the adjective AUGUST, stressed on the second syllable, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is a city in the US state of Georgia, famous for its golf tournament.

clue.text: Specialized hospital in pleasant surroundings?

indicators.note: in tells us the hospital letter sits within the pleasant word
surroundings confirms the pleasant word wraps round the hospital letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A specialist hospital set in agreeable grounds, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Niche as an adjective describes a specialized market or interest catering to a small group.

clue.text: Activated with second reset

indicators.note: reset suggests the letters are set again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Something was turned on, along with a second reboot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' fits the technology picture but signals a rearrangement of WITH SECOND.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch a device on is to activate it, so the phrasal verb matches in sense and tense.

clue.text: Sheer and occasionally delicate part of a car

indicators.note: occasionally means take only some letters, here every other one of the two words Sheer and

parts.note: light means delicate, as in a light touch

explanation.surface: A description of a fine fabric, sheer and sometimes delicate.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of SHEER AND give HEAD; 'Sheer' looks like the start of a fabric description.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlights are the front lamps on a vehicle, a component of it.

clue.text: Various ashtrays emptied — problem solved!

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of the word ashtrays is removed, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: sorted is a colloquial exclamation for a problem fixed

explanation.surface: Several ashtrays have been cleared out, a job neatly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted!' is British slang meaning all fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of mixed kinds, a synonym for various.

clue.text: Plant erasing non-users initially from restored computer system

indicators.note: erasing tells us a letter is wiped out of the word Plant
initially picks the first letter of non-users
restored suggests the letters of from are put back together in another order

explanation.surface: A factory deletes inactive accounts from a rebuilt computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erasing' removes N, the first letter of 'non-users', from PLANT to leave PLAT; 'restored' rearranges FROM as FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform is the underlying hardware or operating environment on which software runs.

clue.text: Feels weird grabbing one personal photo

indicators.note: grabbing means the rearranged letters hold the one inside them
weird suggests the letters of Feels are put into a strange new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone feels odd about taking a single private picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' turns FEELS into SELFE, and 'grabbing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph a person takes of themselves, typically with a phone.

clue.text: Gun rule read out

indicators.note: read out means the answer is the sound of the word for rule when spoken

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle

explanation.surface: A firearms regulation is announced aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy gun, typically mounted on wheels.

clue.text: Parties seen round university and its grounds

indicators.note: seen round means the parties word is placed round the university letter

parts.note: camps are factions or parties

explanation.surface: Groups are spotted around a university and its land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the university, so the definition borrows a word from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Place for pool, say, up for discussion

definitions.meaning: pool, like snooker, is a game played on a table
a proposal ... is open to debate

explanation.surface: Where a game of pool happens is also where an offer is waiting to be debated.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a cue game is played upon a table; idiomatically, an item there is being considered.

clue.text: Talk about a long story!

indicators.note: about indicates the word for talk is turned round

parts.note: gas is informal for chatter, idle talk

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a tediously long tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long, involved narrative, originally a Norse heroic tale.

clue.text: Work steadily, hosting a performance

indicators.note: hosting means the word for working steadily holds the letter a within it

parts.note: to ply is to work at something steadily, as in plying a trade

explanation.surface: Someone keeps working while putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a dramatic work staged before an audience, a theatrical performance.

clue.text: Old character featuring in multi-author narrative

indicators.note: featuring in signals that the answer appears within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: An ageing figure appears in a story written by several people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a person in the story, but it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is a runic letter of Old English and Icelandic, an old written character for th.

clue.text: At first, nobody usually notices she might have a habit

indicators.note: At first means take the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A secret vice that goes unspotted by most people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' hints at an addiction but means a religious robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun wears a habit, the long robe of her religious order.

clue.text: Plait rearranged around one girl's head?

definitions.text: Plait rearranged around one girl's head?

indicators.note: around means the reshuffled letters go round the next pieces
rearranged tells us the letters of Plait are put in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word girl's

explanation.surface: A braid restyled on a girl's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' turns PLAIT into PTAIL, and 'around' puts I plus G inside it; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigtail is a plait of hair hanging from the back or side of the head.

clue.text: Calls for demos: and for nothing

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another, here the word and in place of nothing

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A campaigner urges protests, and for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: In DEMOS, the O (nothing) is swapped for AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand something is to insist on it, to call for it, in the same verb form.

clue.text: Emotional time before New Year

indicators.note: before places the time letter ahead of the rest
New suggests the letters of Year are made over in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Feeling tearful in the run-up to the New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Year' reads as the holiday, but 'New' signals the anagram of YEAR into EARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Teary means tearful, on the verge of crying, an emotional state.
